guides.summary: From your first sign-in to a checked pay schedule, a pilot team and your first published shift.

sections.title: Your first setup checklist
sections.intro: Set the foundations before you invite the whole team. A short, controlled start makes the first working week easier.
blocks: steps

Confirm your access. Use the Business Owner account supplied for your business. Check that the business name is yours and that you can see Business and Payroll. A standard Manager account has different access.

Check the package. Confirm Clockx or Full Workspace, the employee allowance and any enabled add-ons. Ask DayRidge to correct the account configuration before building a workflow around a missing feature.
Set the business basics. Review your business details, pay frequency, payday rule, weekly labour budget and automatic unpaid-break rule. Save, then check the calculated pay-period preview.
Add a small pilot team. Check names, employee numbers, working patterns, start dates and access emails. Add your Managers separately from employee shift profiles.
Run one complete shift. Publish a shift, confirm the employee can see it, record clock-in and clock-out, review breaks and check the resulting worked hours.
Roll out to the rest of the team. Explain who handles questions, when rotas are published and how leave and corrections should be requested.
note
A useful first-day success measure
One employee can sign in, see a published shift, record attendance and find their hours. You can review that record from the owner workspace.
mint

sections.title: Set the business up correctly
sections.intro: These settings influence how the workspace identifies the business and how it presents budgets, pay periods and worked-time estimates.
blocks: steps
Review business details. Enter the business name, trading name, address, business email and phone number. Save a suitable business logo if you want one shown across supported areas.
Choose pay frequency. Select Weekly, Fortnightly, Four-weekly or Monthly. For weekly pay, choose the payday weekday. For monthly pay, choose the day of the month.
Set an anchor where required. Fortnightly and four-weekly cycles need an anchor payday so future paydays can repeat on the intended cycle.
Check the preview. Review the next payday and pay-period dates before saving. Weekly cycles use the previous complete Monday-Sunday week; the monthly preview pays the previous calendar month.
Set the weekly labour budget. Use a positive amount that reflects your planning budget. Budget estimates support rota planning; they are not the final payroll total.
p
If a chosen monthly payday does not exist in a particular month, the app uses that month’s last day. A business logo must be PNG, JPG or WebP and no larger than 2 MB.
note
Two settings to check separately
Automatic breaks are covered later in this guide. The annual leave year is managed by DayRidge administration: ask for the correct January-December or April-March policy to be configured.
lilac

guides.title: Rotas: plan, publish and manage the week
guides.summary: Create and edit shifts, check clashes and leave, publish the rota, review budgets and use the month calendar.
guides.keywords: rota rotas schedule scheduling shifts draft publish published month calendar cover budget conflict clash

sections.title: Build the working week
sections.intro: The rota is a plan for who should work and when. It is separate from the record of hours actually worked.
blocks: steps
Choose the week. Use the week arrows or This week. Check the dates displayed above the board before adding shifts.
Add a shift. Use Add a shift or the plus control in a person’s day cell. Choose the employee, date, start and end times and role details shown in the form.
Work in draft. Draft shifts let you prepare the plan before employees see it. Check coverage, repeated entries and the correct people.
Review availability and leave. Approved leave appears on the board and blocks conflicting additions. Resolve a mismatch rather than forcing a shift onto an unavailable person.
Check the labour picture. The owner can review planned hours and estimated costs against the weekly budget. Open shifts can contribute to planning totals where that tool is available.
Publish when ready. Use the publishing control for the relevant week. Ask one employee to confirm the published shift appears in their personal view.
note
Draft is not published
A saved draft is still a planning record. It does not give employees a published shift. Check the published status after saving and after editing.
mint

sections.title: Publish, correct and find cover
sections.intro: Check the impact of a change before saving it. A clear process prevents the rota, employee expectations and actual attendance from drifting apart.
blocks: flow
Prepare draft
Check conflicts
Publish
Review actual time
bullets
Editing a shift: open the shift chip and check the employee, date and times before saving. If you are changing an already communicated plan, tell the affected employee through your normal process.
Overlapping shifts: the app blocks clashes. Check whether the person already has another shift and whether the date or overnight end time is wrong.
Approved leave: do not work around a leave clash by creating a duplicate employee. Review the leave decision and intended dates first.
Removing a shift: read the confirmation and distinguish a planned rota shift from a completed worked-time entry. Removing a plan should not be treated as correcting a clocking record.
Sickness cover: supported Full Workspace rota controls can create an open cover offer for an eligible upcoming published shift. Review the absence and the dates first.
note
Check the result in both places
After a material change, review the manager rota and the employee’s published schedule. Use Activity to see recorded management changes and to help resolve questions.
lilac

sections.title: Read the shift calendar
sections.intro: The month calendar brings planned work, recorded shifts and time away into a clear date-based view. Select a date for the underlying detail.
sections.where: Employee > My shifts / Rota > Month calendar
blocks: visual
calendar
steps
Choose whose calendar to view. In the Manager rota month view, select the team member. Employees see their own schedule.
Move between months. Use the left and right arrows. Today returns you to the current date. The month changes directly; it is not a native month-selection wheel.
Read the key. Green shows upcoming or completed shifts, orange overtime and purple time away such as approved holiday or recorded sickness. Split colours show more than one type on the same date.
Select a day. Read the listed times and status rather than drawing conclusions from the colour alone. A past scheduled shift is not proof that the employee actually clocked in.
Refresh when needed. Use the refresh control after a recent decision or correction. Check that the month and person still match the record you intended to review.
note
Example illustration
The calendar above illustrates the colour key. Your actual dates, shift totals and details come from the records and permissions in your workspace.
lilac

sections.title: Common rota questions
sections.intro: Start with the person, dates and status before trying the same change again.
blocks: table
Question
What to check
Why can an employee not see a shift?
Check the employee record and week, then confirm that the shift is published. Drafts are for planning.
Why can I not add a shift?
Check for approved leave, overlapping shifts and the employee selected in the form.
Does publishing record hours worked?
No. Published shifts describe the plan; clockings and authorised worked-time entries record actual attendance.
Do I have to use the month picker?
No. Left and right arrows change the calendar month directly. Select a date to read its details.
Can a Team Leader change the rota?
Only if the owner grants Manage the team rota. Their supported controls are more focused than the Manager workspace.
note
Before you finish
Review the correct week, published status and employee view. Tell affected staff about material changes through your normal communication process.

sections.title: If a shift looks wrong
sections.intro: Your personal calendar reflects the records shared with your account.
blocks: steps
Check the date and month, including whether the shift runs overnight.
Select the day and read the status and times. A past scheduled shift does not prove that a clock-in was recorded.
Ask your Manager about a missing or incorrect plan. Draft rota changes are not visible as published shifts.
For actual worked hours, check your clocking history or My hours. Ask for a correction if the recorded attendance is wrong.

guides.title: Manage clocking, kiosks and breaks
guides.summary: Set up the shared kiosk, review active staff and correct worked time without deducting a break twice.
guides.keywords: clock clocking kiosk pin missed shift break automatic unpaid edit correction worked hours

sections.title: Set up and use the kiosk
sections.intro: The kiosk is the shared workplace clocking view. It uses employee numbers and personal PINs, with manager access protected by a separate kiosk PIN.
blocks: steps
Choose the workplace device. Open the correct business workspace and enter the workplace kiosk through the supported manager control.
Complete device setup if requested. Use the manager setup flow for the workplace device. Confirm the business shown is the one whose staff will use it.
Keep manager access private. The manager kiosk PIN is six digits. Store and communicate it only to the people who should unlock or exit the protected kiosk.
Explain employee clocking. Employees enter their own employee number and personal PIN, then follow the clock-in or clock-out flow shown on the device.
Check a real result. After a pilot clocking, confirm the correct employee appears in the team clock status. At the end, confirm the completed record and break information.
bullets
Do not use one employee number for several staff.
Do not leave the owner’s private dashboard open on the shared kiosk.
If a clocking fails, check the number, PIN and device state before creating another employee.
note
Kiosk and personal clocking are different routes
Employees may also have My Time Clock in their signed-in account. Explain which route your business expects them to use.
lilac

sections.title: Clock in, clock out and check
sections.intro: Published shifts describe the plan. Successful clock-ins and clock-outs create the worked-time record used in attendance and payroll-hour summaries.
sections.where: My Time Clock / Manager > Time clock
blocks: steps
Employee starts work. Use the personal clocking page or workplace kiosk. Wait for the app to confirm the clock-in; an unsaved tap is not a recorded shift.
Employee checks the active shift. My Time Clock shows whether they are clocked in, the elapsed timer and a current earnings estimate where available.
Manager checks the team. Use the team clock status to review who is working. The manager’s own personal shift should use their linked employee profile.
Employee finishes work. Choose Clock out and complete the confirmation. Check the result rather than leaving the page during saving.

Resolve a missed clocking. An authorised Manager can clock an employee in or out and adjust the relevant time through supported manager controls. Record the actual agreed time, not a convenient default.
note
A connection problem after clock-in

A clock-in already saved to DayRidge is not erased because the page closes or briefly becomes unavailable. When access returns, refresh and check the active record. A failed or unconfirmed new action still needs review.
lilac
p
The elapsed timer and earnings display are live estimates. Unpaid breaks and authorised corrections can change the final worked hours.

sections.title: Break rules and time corrections
sections.intro: Review recorded breaks and saved automatic rules together. The same break should not be deducted twice.
blocks: visual
hours
bullets
Configure new shifts: in Business, set whether automatic unpaid breaks are enabled, the shift length that must be exceeded and the unpaid minutes to apply.
Understand the saved rule: new clock-ins and manually added shifts use the current rule. Existing shifts keep the rule saved with them; changing today’s setting does not rewrite every old record.
Compare manual and automatic breaks: where a longer recorded break exists, that value is used. Review the displayed total unpaid break rather than adding the two deductions together.
Correct a completed shift: find the employee’s past shift, use Edit, review start, end and unpaid break, then save. Check overnight dates carefully.
Delete only an erroneous entry: read the confirmation and check the employee and dates. A genuine worked shift normally needs a correction rather than deletion.
note
Check before payroll
The example shows 8 elapsed hours less a 30-minute unpaid break, giving 7.5 paid hours. Your business rule and the actual saved record determine the real result.
mint

guides.title: Manage annual leave and balances
guides.summary: Review requests, check cover and estimated hours, record decisions and undo supported upcoming approvals.
guides.keywords: holiday annual leave approve approval decline balance entitlement request undo cancel

sections.title: Review holiday requests clearly
sections.intro: Check the requested dates, the employee’s balance and the effect on cover before making a decision.
blocks: steps
Open the pending request. Check the person, start date, end date and the estimated leave hours. Compare the request with the rota and existing leave.
Review the balance. Check start date, working pattern and contracted hours. Estimates depend on the employee inputs, recorded information and the configured leave year.
Approve or decline. Save the decision using the request controls and verify the new status. Approved leave reduces the available balance and blocks rota shifts on those dates.
Undo an upcoming approval when needed. Use the undo/cancellation action where available and read the confirmation. Check the request and balance again after it saves.
Resolve year-boundary requests. Split a request that crosses the leave-year boundary into the appropriate periods rather than assuming a single total belongs to one year.
h
The owner’s review
p

The displayed entitlement is an estimate to review alongside your business’s agreed terms. If the balance is surprising, check the underlying employee record and dates first. Ask DayRidge to correct the configured leave year if it is wrong.
note
Permission-based delegation
Full Workspace Team Leaders can review leave only if the owner grants that permission. Sickness is a separate record and does not deduct annual leave.
lilac

guides.title: Record sickness and return to work
guides.summary: Keep absence dates up to date, mark the actual return and review date-only absence trends.
guides.keywords: sick sickness absence absent return returned ongoing analytics

sections.title: Record sickness and the return
sections.intro: Keep absence dates accurate and separate from holiday approval. An expected return is a planning date; an actual return closes the absence record.
blocks: steps
Record the absence. Identify the employee and first day absent. Enter the supported expected-return information if it is known.
Review ongoing records. Use the Ongoing filter to identify who is still off. An absence past the expected date needs follow-up; it should not be assumed to have ended.
Update dates when the position changes. Use Edit dates to correct the supported absence details. Keep the expected return realistic for planning purposes.
Mark the employee returned. When they return, use Mark returned and save the actual return date. Complete the return-to-work discussion and follow-up fields shown in that workflow.
Review date-only trends. Use the absence overview’s date range to see aggregate patterns. Check the selected period before comparing totals.
note
Record dates, not diagnoses

The sickness workspace is designed for restricted absence dates and return information. Do not enter diagnoses or other medical detail into operational notes. Sickness is recorded, not approved, and does not reduce annual leave.
lilac
p
If absence affects a future rota shift, review cover separately. Do not edit a sickness record merely to make a staffing total look correct.

guides.title: Manage people, onboarding and permissions
guides.summary: Add employees and management accounts, review starter information and control access to personal records.
guides.keywords: people employee employees onboarding invitation manager team leader permissions private bank details profile photo

sections.title: Give each person the right view
sections.intro: The Business Owner is the primary business manager account. It is distinct from the DayRidge platform administrator who manages the service.
blocks: table
Role
Main purpose
Key boundary
Business Owner / General Manager
Business settings, team oversight, payroll and access control
Owner-level access to wage and gross-pay reporting
Manager
Plan rotas, review requests and manage worked-time records
Team payroll and wage reporting stay with the owner
Team Leader
Published shifts and individually granted team tools
No private employee files, bank details or payroll
Employee
Own shifts, attendance, leave and personal information
Own records; extra tools depend on the package
h
Understand the three access checks
bullets
Package: does the business have this tool?
Add-on: has DayRidge enabled the purchased extra?
Person: does this account have the role or permission needed?
p

A Manager who also works shifts may have a linked employee profile and a My shifts & pay switch. Management access and an employee shift record serve different purposes; an employee profile uses an employee place in the business allowance.
note
Delegate deliberately
Give people the smallest set of permissions that lets them do their job. Revisit access when responsibilities change or someone leaves.
mint

sections.title: Invite Managers and Team Leaders
sections.intro: Create a clear management structure before handing over the working week. Access changes should match the responsibility you intend to delegate.
blocks: steps
Choose the account type. The Business Owner can invite a full Manager. A Team Leader is a more limited account with focused permissions.
Enter the person’s name and email. Use an address they can access. Send the invitation and check that the management list reflects the expected account.
Set Team Leader permissions. The owner chooses extra access when inviting a Team Leader or uses Edit access afterwards. New extra permissions start off unless selected.
Review the actual experience. Ask the person to refresh their workspace and confirm that the expected sections appear.
Remove access when appropriate. Use the relevant Remove action after checking which account and role you are removing. Do not remove the wrong person simply because names are similar.
h
Team Leader options
bullets
View team directory: active staff names and roles.
View open shifts and daily attendance totals, without wages.
Manage the team rota: draft shifts and individual publication.
Review annual leave: decisions and undoing upcoming approvals.
note
Private access stays separate
Team Leader permissions do not expose private employee files or payroll. Full Workspace personnel permissions and Stock permissions have their own controls.
lilac

sections.title: Add and maintain employee records
sections.intro: A reliable employee record connects rota planning, clocking, leave and payroll hours. Check the basics rather than rushing through account creation.
blocks: steps

Enter the employee’s identity. Check their name, role and account email. Use the employee number assigned in the business and give them their personal clocking PIN through an appropriate private channel.
Set employment inputs carefully. Review start date, regular or irregular working pattern and contracted hours or days where required. These inputs affect leave estimates and other summaries.
Check owner-only pay information. The owner should verify the hourly rate used for estimates. Standard Managers and Team Leaders do not receive team wage reporting.
Decide whether onboarding is required. If you already hold the information, do not ask the employee to complete the same form unnecessarily. Use the option available in the creation flow.
Confirm setup. Check the new record appears, the invitation has reached the correct person and they can see their own workspace.
h
Plan limits and departures
p

Adding a person beyond the approved employee allowance can require DayRidge approval. Use the account’s upgrade/request route rather than creating duplicate records. Archiving a leaver and deleting an unused setup record are different actions; read the confirmation before proceeding.
note
Before the first live shift
Check the employee number and PIN on the actual workplace device. Fix account mismatches before people start using each other’s records.
mint

sections.title: Onboard a new starter
sections.intro: Onboarding gathers starter information for authorised review. It can be required or marked unnecessary when the business already has what it needs.
blocks: flow
Set requirement
Employee submits
Owner reviews
Confirm outcome
steps
Explain what is needed. Tell the employee whether the onboarding form is required and where to find it. The form can contain identity, address, starter-tax and bank information.
Employee completes the form. They review the requested fields and submit it. A submitted form is awaiting review; submission alone is not owner approval.
Review the information. Use the Onboarding workspace to check the employee and the status. Confirm the information matches the person you intended to onboard.
Approve or request changes. Follow the available review controls. If something is incomplete, explain what needs correcting rather than approving an uncertain record.
Complete your business process. Make sure your approved personnel and payroll process has the information it needs. Do not treat the submitted form as a substitute for a maintained employee file.
note
Know the status
Not required, Not started, Awaiting review, Approved and Changes requested describe different stages. Check the status after saving instead of assuming a form has been accepted.
lilac

sections.title: Employee files and personal changes
sections.intro: Keep personal information under the right access controls. An employee can propose changes to their own details; authorised people review the request.
blocks: steps
Open the correct record. Use Employee files and identify the employee before reviewing contact, emergency or other personnel information.
Review incoming changes. Employees use My details to submit changes to supported contact and bank fields. Check the proposed values before approving a request.
Separate bank-related access. Review the permission controls carefully; bank information is more sensitive than a team directory entry.
Manage delegated access. The Business Owner controls which authorised Managers can access or approve protected personnel information. Give access only where their role requires it.
Review profile photos. Employee profile-photo submissions can await an authorised manager’s decision before appearing to the team.
h
Explain this to employees
p

Submitting a change does not mean the business has accepted it. Employees should check the status and tell the owner promptly about time-sensitive changes. A contact-information update does not automatically decide or complete a payroll change.
note
A team list is not a personnel file
The team directory is for operational names and roles. It should not be used to circulate private personal, bank or onboarding information.
mint

guides.title: Contracts, policies and read receipts
guides.summary: Share the right document with the right audience and understand acknowledgement, drafts and archiving.
guides.keywords: contract contracts policy policies documents upload read receipt acknowledge signature

sections.title: Share contracts and policies
sections.intro: Choose the correct audience before sharing. A company document and a private employee contract are not the same kind of record.
blocks: steps
Choose the document type. Prepare a private employee contract or upload a company document. Select the intended employee when using private scope.
Prepare the content. Use the contract editor or upload an existing supported file. Give it a clear title and description. Supported uploads include PDF, DOCX, PNG and JPG up to 10 MB.

Check the sharing choice. Leave Share now off to save a draft. Company documents shared with the business are visible to active members; private employee documents are limited to the selected employee and authorised management.
Choose acknowledgement. Decide whether staff must mark the document as read. A review date, or a certificate expiry date where that category is used, helps identify records that need attention.
Review receipts and lifecycle. Open the document to see recorded read receipts. Drafts can be edited or deleted. Shared documents can be archived or restored through supported controls.
note
Receipt is not a signature
A contract’s Acknowledge receipt action records that the employee received/read it. It does not sign the contract or accept its terms. Use your own approved signing process when one is needed.
lilac
p
Archived company documents leave the staff library. Employees retain access to their own previous contracts, and read receipts remain recorded.

sections.title: Employees: read your own documents
sections.intro: Your Documents area shows company documents and employee documents shared with your account.
blocks: steps
Open Documents and choose the item you need. Use View document and check the title and version/context before reading.
Read the document or download the available file. DOCX files may need downloading to open.
If acknowledgement is requested, tick I have read this document after reading it and use Mark as read or Acknowledge receipt.
Check that receipt is recorded. Contract acknowledgement records receipt; it does not sign or accept the contract terms.

guides.title: Review and export payroll hours
guides.summary: Check pay periods, worked time, breaks and owner-only gross estimates before the payroll handover.
guides.keywords: pay payroll paid hours csv export salary wage wages gross earnings rate period

sections.title: Prepare hours for payroll
sections.intro: Use DayRidge to review recorded hours and gross estimates, then hand the checked information to your normal payroll process.
blocks: steps
Check the pay schedule. Review the owner’s Business settings and the period being reported. A wrong anchor or monthly day can put otherwise correct shifts in the wrong view.
Review every employee. Check missing clock-outs, duplicate shifts, unexpected durations and unpaid breaks. Resolve the underlying attendance record before relying on a total.
Review hourly rates. Confirm the owner-only employee pay inputs are correct. A changed rate or correction can affect estimated gross amounts.
Use the supported export. Export the recorded attendance/payroll hours through the available CSV control and check the downloaded period and employee numbers.

Finish payroll in your established process. Apply the business’s approved payroll rules, deductions and final checks outside the worked-hours review. Keep an agreed copy of the export you actually used.
h
Know the boundary
p
Gross earnings estimates are not take-home pay. DayRidge’s time and pay summaries do not calculate every tax, pension, statutory payment or adjustment, and they do not issue payslips.
note
Access is intentional
Business payroll and team wage reporting belong to the Business Owner. Employees see their own information; standard Managers and Team Leaders do not receive team payroll access.
lilac

guides.title: Tasks and shared shift checklists
guides.summary: Assign work, build reusable checklists, let staff take ownership and capture live photo evidence.
guides.keywords: task tasks checklist checklists camera photo evidence ownership take task claim complete completed to do progress opening closing

sections.title: Assign individual work
sections.intro: Use individual tasks when a particular employee needs a clear action, instructions and deadline. Use shared shift checklists for a job that only needs doing once.
blocks: steps
Confirm activation. Tasks is a paid add-on for Full Workspace. Ask DayRidge to enable it for the purchasing business and confirm the agreed chargeable-user count.
Create the task. Enter a concise title, useful instructions and a due date where needed. Explain what finished work should look like.
Assign the right people. Select the intended employee or employees. For individual assignments, each person’s progress is tracked separately.
Employee progresses the work. In My Tasks, they review instructions and move their own assignment through To do, In progress and Complete using the available controls.
Review the result. Use the manager view to check completion and overdue work. Follow up on missing work through the business’s normal management process.
table
Use individual tasks for
Use shift checklists for
A named employee’s specific job
A shared opening, closing or shift check
A personal deadline or follow-up
One task claimed by one person from eligible shifts
Separate progress per assignment
Structured answers and optional required live photos
note
Keep the task list useful
Give tasks a clear owner and sensible due date. Avoid repeating a shared job as multiple individual assignments when the team only needs it completed once.
mint

sections.title: Build a reusable shift checklist
sections.intro: A checklist template defines the job. Allocating it to published shifts creates a shared task for that working day.
blocks: flow
Create template
Select shifts
One person claims
Review completion
steps
Create the template. Give the checklist a title and instructions. Examples include opening checks, a handover or a close-down routine.
Add structured fields. Choose checkboxes, text answers, numbers or selection options. Mark the fields that are required and make question wording specific enough to answer consistently.
Choose evidence requirements. Enable Require photo evidence where the job genuinely benefits from a fresh photograph. Do not require unnecessary images of people or private information.
Allocate to the shift. Choose the saved template, the working date and the relevant published employee shifts. Publish the rota first if no shifts are available.
Check the shared run. The selected shift group shares a checklist that only needs completing once. The board shows Available, In progress or Completed, who took it and the relevant timestamps.
note
Completion is recorded, not a separate approval stage
Managers can inspect answers, evidence and completion details. Do not describe this as an appraisal, electronic signature or a separate manager sign-off workflow.
lilac

sections.title: Take ownership and finish the job
sections.intro: Employees can claim an available shared shift task, complete the required answers and capture fresh evidence in the app.
blocks: steps
Choose active work. The active view shows new and in-progress work. Completed tasks are available in their separate view instead of sitting under the main list.
Take the task. Open an available checklist and choose Take task. Check that your name appears as the person who has taken it. Other colleagues can see that it is already owned.
Answer the checklist. Read the instructions and complete required fields. Use the right units for numeric answers and explain relevant exceptions in supported text fields.

Take live evidence where needed. Choose Take photo, allow camera access and capture the scene in the branded camera dialog. Gallery uploads are disabled in this workflow. Required-photo checklists need at least one live image.
Complete or release. Submit completion when the job is finished. If you cannot do it, use the supported release action to return the task to the board rather than leaving it claimed indefinitely.
p

A checklist can hold up to five photos. If the camera is blocked, review the browser’s camera permission for the DayRidge app and try again. Capture the task itself; a fresh photo does not replace a manager’s review of the actual work.
note
Manager follow-up
Inspect the recorded answers, claimant and time, and open evidence photos where needed. Use the Completed tasks area to find finished work.
mint

guides.title: Stock counts, takings and investigations
guides.summary: Create consistent products, run stocktakes, reconcile till figures and explain differences.
guides.keywords: stock stocks stocktake stocktakes count counts till takings reconciliation waste delivery deliveries variance short over difference delete restore

sections.title: Set up products and permissions
sections.intro: Start with consistent product records. Accurate units and prices matter more than a long product list with inconsistent assumptions.
blocks: steps
Confirm the add-on. Stock Management must be active for the business. The owner or authorised access manager controls which Managers can use it.
Create a product. Use Add product and enter a clear name, product code or category where relevant, counting unit, purchase cost and selling price.

Choose one usable unit. Count the same product in the same unit throughout opening counts, deliveries, waste and closing stock. Decide whether a unit means an item, bottle, measure or another supported unit.
Review prices. Keep purchase costs, selling prices and till figures on a consistent tax and pricing basis chosen by the business.
Check operational access. Give count-entry access to the appropriate Managers. Delegate access-management permission only where it is needed.
h
Explain the counting rules
p

Write down any business-specific unit convention before the first stocktake. If stock is bought in one pack size but sold in another, decide and consistently apply the conversion you will enter. The app does not automatically turn recipes, portions or yields into stock units.
note
Manual figures, matched periods
This version uses entered counts, movements and till amounts. Do not assume it is connected directly to your till or that it imports sales automatically.
lilac

sections.title: Run a stocktake you can trust
sections.intro: A useful stocktake compares physical counts and relevant movements over the same period as the till sales being reviewed.
blocks: steps
Start the record. Choose New stocktake and give the period a recognisable title. Check opening and closing count times before entering figures.
Confirm the opening position. Enter the first opening count where needed or check the supported opening balance carried from the preceding record.
Record movements. Account for deliveries, waste, complimentary items and relevant adjustments using consistent product units. Give a reason when a correction or non-sale movement needs one.
Count closing stock. Enter what is physically present at the closing point. Recheck an unusually high or low quantity before relying on calculated usage.
Match the sales period. Enter the relevant till sales for exactly the same period and products. Avoid comparing a whole-day till total with a partial-shift count.
Save or complete. Save unfinished work as a draft, then reopen it when you can finish. Review the count and sales comparisons before completing the stocktake.
note
History matters
Keep stocktakes in a sensible chronological sequence. Later records can depend on an earlier closing count. Review dependencies before deleting or changing a linked record.
lilac

sections.title: Explain stock and till differences
sections.intro: Use differences to start a review of the underlying figures. A variance is a signal to investigate, not an automatic explanation of what happened.
blocks: visual
stock
steps
Check the sign. Difference is recorded till sales minus expected sales. A negative amount is short; a positive amount is over.
Check the inputs first. Review count dates, units, deliveries, waste, complimentary items, adjustments and selling prices. Recount where appropriate.
Record an investigation note. Identify the product or whole stocktake, explain the discrepancy and keep an actionable follow-up. Use the supported open/resolved state.
Use analytics carefully. Choose the reporting period before comparing usage, sales or product performance. Make sure the included stocktakes are comparable.
Handle deleted records deliberately. Deleted stocktakes can be viewed and restored through Show deleted stocktakes. Later stocktakes that depend on the closing count must be dealt with first.
note
Keep the interpretation fair
A short figure may come from a count, price, timing or entry issue. Check the evidence before deciding what action the business should take.
mint

guides.title: Activity, notifications and daily routines

sections.title: Use Activity and notifications
sections.intro: A good review starts with the underlying record. Notifications help you notice work; Activity helps you understand recorded management changes.
blocks: steps
Open Activity. Review the recorded actor, summary and time for changes such as rota publishing, timesheet edits, requests and settings.
Filter by category. Use All activity, Rota, Timesheets, Requests, Team or Settings to narrow the question you are investigating.
Open the relevant workspace. Compare the activity entry with the current shift, request or employee record. A historical event and a current status can both be correct.
Use the bell as an inbox. Read the notification and follow its link to the work that needs attention. Marking a notification as read does not approve the underlying request.
Confirm the actual outcome. Check the saved request status, published shift or corrected worked-time record after taking action.
h
Questions Activity can help answer
bullets
Who published or amended the rota?
When was a timesheet corrected?
Was a request decision recorded?
Did someone change the business settings?
note
Business oversight versus DayRidge administration
Your business account does not include DayRidge’s provider finance console, website-traffic dashboard or management of other customers. Ask DayRidge about your subscription or service account.
lilac

sections.title: A simple operating rhythm
sections.intro: Use a repeatable routine so important records are checked at the right time rather than only when somebody raises a problem.
blocks: table
When
Review
A good outcome

Today’s rota, expected staff, ongoing sickness, open cover and active tasks
The team knows who is working and what needs doing

Keep an owner for every review
Decide who checks the rota, who corrects time, who reviews leave and who prepares payroll. Delegation works best when each task has a clear person and a clear deadline.

sections.title: Access, invitations and devices
sections.intro: Start with the message on screen. Fix the actual account or device issue rather than creating duplicate staff or repeatedly retrying the same action.
sections.where: Sign in / Managers / Team / My Tasks
blocks: table
What you see
What to check
No invitation or setup email
Check the recorded email, junk folder and latest resend result. Use the supported setup resend action; do not create another person just to trigger another message.
Password reset is not working
Use the branded app address and the latest recovery email. Request a new link through Forgot password if the old one is no longer valid.
Payroll or Business is missing
Confirm this is the Business Owner account. A standard Manager or Team Leader does not have these owner-only sections.
Tasks or Stock is missing
Confirm Full Workspace, add-on activation and the person’s permission. Ask DayRidge to check the business entitlement if necessary.
The employee cannot see a shift
Check the employee, week/month and published status. A draft is not an employee-visible published shift.
Camera cannot open for a checklist
Check browser camera permission for the app, device camera availability and the on-screen message. Refresh after changing permission. Gallery upload is not the live-evidence route.
Business access is paused
Ask the owner to contact DayRidge about the business account. Repeated password resets do not change its service status.
note
When asking for help
Give the business name, affected screen, approximate time, exact error and what you expected. Avoid sending passwords, PINs, bank details or unnecessary employee information.
lilac

sections.title: Hours, balances and stock totals
sections.intro: Unexpected totals usually need a review of inputs, dates and record status. Check those before making a correction.
blocks: table
Question
Check in this order
Why is a shift total wrong?
Employee and date; clock-in/out; overnight end date; manual break; saved automatic-break rule; duplicate worked-time entries.
Why does the rota differ from hours?
A rota is a plan; attendance records what was saved as worked time. Review the actual clockings and any authorised corrections.
Why is an earnings estimate different?
Recorded hours, unpaid breaks, rate and pay period. Gross estimates exclude payroll deductions and are not net pay.
Why is the leave balance unexpected?
Employee start date, regular/irregular pattern, contracted hours, configured leave year, approved leave and the request dates.
Why is sickness still ongoing?
An expected return date does not close the record. Check whether an actual return was saved through Mark returned.
Why can nobody take a checklist?
Check the allocated published shifts and whether a colleague has already claimed it. Use release when it needs returning to the board.
Why is stock showing a difference?
Opening/closing times and units; physical counts; movements; prices; till period and entered sales. Check like-for-like figures.
note
After a correction
Refresh and check the source record, the affected total and any export you intend to use. Keep a note of the business reason where the workflow provides one.
mint

sections.title: Set up your account

Open the latest account-setup email sent to the address your Manager has recorded for you. Complete the password setup flow.
Sign in at app.dayridge.co.uk and check that the workspace belongs to your employer. Use your own login.
Open My shifts to check your published work. Your employee number and kiosk PIN are separate from your email/password sign-in.
Ask your Manager whether to use the workplace kiosk or My Time Clock. Wait for a confirmation whenever you clock in or out.
Use the leave route available in your package to request holiday. A request is not approved until the decision is recorded.
Complete onboarding only if your employer requires it. Ask your business about any field you do not understand.

Your own information
You can see your own records and documents shared with you. Management pages, other employees’ private information and team payroll are not part of your employee account.

guides.title: Clock in and out as an employee
guides.summary: Record your own attendance, check the active shift and understand the timer and earnings estimate.
guides.keywords: employee personal phone clock in out earnings timer live time kiosk pin

sections.title: Record the working day
sections.intro: A rota is the plan. A successful clocking action records attendance.
blocks: steps
Follow your employer’s chosen clocking route. In My Time Clock, sign in with your own account. At the kiosk, use your own employee number and personal PIN.
Choose the clock-in action when you start work and wait for confirmation. Check that the page shows Clocked in.
In My Time Clock, check the recorded start time and elapsed timer. Current earnings is a gross estimate that can change with breaks and corrections.
When you finish, choose Clock out and complete the confirmation. Wait for the saved result.
Review recent clockings or My hours. If the record is wrong, tell your Manager the actual date, start/end times and relevant break.
note
If the page briefly goes down
A clock-in already saved is not erased by closing the page or a brief outage. Refresh when access returns and check the record. A failed or unconfirmed new action still needs checking.

sections.title: Avoid common mistakes
sections.intro: Keep the account and the action personal.
blocks: bullets
Do not use another employee’s number, PIN or account.
Do not assume a published rota shift automatically recorded a clock-in.
Do not repeatedly tap during saving; wait for the outcome.
Do not treat gross estimated earnings as final take-home pay.
Ask your Manager to review missed clockings and breaks rather than inventing a replacement record.

sections.title: When Geo Clock-in is enabled
sections.intro: Some businesses require a workplace location check for personal-phone clock-ins.
blocks: p

Allow a fresh precise-location check when prompted. You must be within the workplace area and have a sufficiently accurate reading. Follow the Geo Clock-in employee guide for the full steps and permission help.

guides.title: Request holiday and report time away

sections.title: Request annual leave
sections.intro: Use your own leave area, then wait for a Manager’s decision.
sections.where: My leave (Clockx) / My shifts request controls (Full Workspace)
blocks: steps
Choose the annual-leave request action in the section available to your account.
Enter the first and last dates you want off, and review the estimated hours and balance shown.
Check the dates carefully, especially if the request crosses your business’s leave-year boundary. Split it into the appropriate periods when required.
Submit the request. Pending means a decision has not yet been recorded.
Return to the request to check whether it is approved or declined. Speak to your Manager before treating requested dates as agreed holiday.
Ask your Manager about changing an approved request. Do not assume removing a note or a calendar entry cancels an approval.
note
If the balance is unexpected
Ask your business to review your start date, contracted hours, working pattern, approved leave and configured leave year. You do not change your employer’s leave policy from the employee account.

sections.title: Keep sickness separate
sections.intro: Full Workspace supports sickness reporting. Your business’s reporting procedure still applies.
blocks: steps
Notify your business through its agreed absence-reporting route.
Use the sickness reporting action where it is available and enter the supported absence dates.
Update your Manager about the expected return and tell them when you actually return.
Do not enter diagnoses or unnecessary medical detail in operational notes. Sickness is separate from annual leave and does not use holiday balance.

guides.title: Set up Geo Clock-in for your workplace
guides.summary: Enable the add-on, set the workplace location and radius, test employee arrival checks and handle Manager overrides.
guides.package: Clockx or Full Workspace + Geo Clock-in add-on
guides.keywords: geo geofence geolocation gps location workplace coordinates latitude longitude radius onsite allow permission precise current location setup

sections.title: Enable access and set the workplace
sections.intro: Geo Clock-in is optional for both packages. Existing businesses are not enrolled automatically.
sections.where: Platform admin > Add-ons > Geo Clock-in; Business Owner > Business profile
blocks: steps
Agree your billing. Geo Clock-in is £4.99 per business per month or £49.99 per business per year. It covers everyone within your agreed employee allowance. Your core subscription is separate.
Enable the business. Your DayRidge platform admin enables Geo Clock-in under Add-ons for the purchasing business. Enabling access does not collect payment.
Open Business profile. The Business Owner finds the Geo Clock-in section. Other Managers cannot change the workplace location.

Set the centre point. While physically at the premises, choose Set location from this device and allow location permission. Alternatively enter accurate workplace latitude and longitude. Check the values before saving.
Choose the radius. Enter a whole distance from 50 to 1,000 metres. Start with 100 metres and test it at the actual premises; device accuracy and building conditions vary.
Save workplace location. Employees can then make personal-phone clock-ins that pass the location check. Until a location is saved, an enabled business cannot accept those clock-ins.
note
Use the workplace location
The device button fills the location of the device you are using. Set it at the premises, or enter the correct workplace coordinates manually. It does not look up the business address automatically.

sections.title: Test the area before staff use it
sections.intro: A short on-site check prevents avoidable clock-in problems on the first working day.
blocks: steps
Explain the check. Tell staff why a current location is requested and how to contact a Manager if it cannot be verified.
Check inside the workplace. Ask a staff member with a real shift starting to test clock-in with precise location allowed. Do not create attendance records purely as a location test.
Review the permitted area. An outside location is rejected. A poor-accuracy fix or one close to the boundary may also be rejected; move closer or retry with a clearer signal.
Adjust if necessary. The Owner can refine the centre and radius in Business profile. Use an area that suits the actual premises.
note
Accuracy and limits
DayRidge checks a fresh device location and its reported accuracy. Device locations can be inaccurate or spoofed. Geo Clock-in is an arrival check, not a guarantee of physical presence.

sections.title: Handle exceptions and permission problems
sections.intro: Keep a clear record when a legitimate arrival needs a Manager to intervene.
sections.where: Business profile / Time clock > Team clock
blocks: steps

Location blocked. Allow location for app.dayridge.co.uk in the browser’s website settings and check the phone’s Location Services and precise-location permission. Refresh DayRidge after changing permissions. An embedded browser may require opening the app directly in Safari or Chrome.
Inaccurate or unavailable location. Check location services, try somewhere with a clearer signal and retry. An expired reading needs a new clock-in attempt.
Record an authorised arrival. A Manager can use the existing team clock action with a reason of at least five characters. The reason stays with the attendance record and its audit history.
Keep kiosk access available. Registered workplace kiosks retain their existing device/PIN flow. Clocking out does not require a location check.
Change access through DayRidge. The platform admin can disable the add-on. Geo access remains available if a business changes between Full Workspace and Clockx.
note
Location privacy
There is no continuous employee tracking. The check happens when a personal-phone clock-in is requested. These Geo functions do not save raw employee coordinates.

guides.title: Clock in with a workplace location check
guides.summary: Allow precise location, clock in when you arrive and understand outside-area or permission messages.
guides.package: Clockx or Full Workspace + Geo Clock-in add-on

sections.title: Clock in when you arrive
sections.intro: Follow these steps when your employer has enabled Geo Clock-in.
blocks: steps
Arrive at your workplace. Open DayRidge on your own phone and sign in to your account.
Choose Clock in. DayRidge requests your current location for this clock-in attempt.
Allow precise location. Accept the browser prompt and make sure the phone’s location services are enabled.
Check the result. The shift starts only after DayRidge accepts the location and records the clock-in. Confirm that the running shift is shown.
note
Only at clock-in
DayRidge does not continuously track your movements. Clocking out does not require location.

sections.title: Understand a blocked clock-in
sections.intro: A failed location check does not start your shift. Speak to your Manager promptly if you have arrived but cannot clock in.
sections.where: My Time Clock / browser website settings / phone location settings
blocks: table
Message
What to do
Outside the workplace area
Arrive at the premises and try again. If you are already there, ask your Manager to check the workplace setup.
Location permission blocked
Allow location for app.dayridge.co.uk in your browser’s website settings. Check phone Location Services and precise-location permission, then refresh.
Poor accuracy or close to the edge
Move closer to the workplace or somewhere with a clearer signal, then retry.
Location expired or timed out
Try again to obtain a fresh reading.
Workplace not set up
Ask your Business Owner or Manager to complete the Geo Clock-in setup.
p
If location still fails, use your employer’s registered workplace kiosk or ask a Manager to record your arrival with a reason. A location error is not proof that someone is absent or late.

sections.title: Finish your shift
sections.intro: The location restriction applies to starting a shift on a personal phone.
blocks: steps
Choose Clock out at the end of the shift and confirm the action.
Check that DayRidge shows the shift as ended.
Ask your Manager to review any attendance correction through the normal workplace process.
